title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
about:
Twelve cases bring Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson from the sitting-room at Baker Street into a world of pawnshops, railway journeys, suburban villas, country houses, and closely guarded family secrets. A royal visitor wants a photograph recovered. A pawnbroker has been paid to copy an encyclopaedia. A young woman arrives with a troubling account of her employment. Again and again, something apparently trivial becomes the detail on which an entire explanation turns.

Watson tells these stories as a friend, witness, and practising doctor. He shares the reader's uncertainty, admires Holmes's ingenuity, and sometimes feels the discomfort of helping him. Holmes can be theatrical, impatient, generous, and mistaken. The pleasures of detection sit beside harder questions: who has the power to tell a convincing story, whose reputation receives protection, and whether finding the truth necessarily means delivering someone to the law. Read each story as its own case, while watching how the friendship and the detective's habits accumulate across the collection.

whyItMatters.title: Evidence needs an explanation
whyItMatters.body: A worn cuff, a hat, a railway journey, or an unusual condition of employment can change the meaning of everything around it. These stories invite us to distinguish a visible fact from the story we tell about it. Holmes's confidence is compelling, but the opening case also gives us reason to examine the assumptions behind it.

whyItMatters.title: Private life has unequal protections
whyItMatters.body: Kings, bankers, governesses, tradesmen, and people living behind respectable appearances come within the same investigative frame. Their ability to protect themselves differs sharply. Money, marriage, employment, and reputation shape what a client can disclose and what another person can make them conceal.

whyItMatters.title: Solving a case is a moral choice
whyItMatters.body: Holmes's discoveries do not all lead to the same kind of ending. Watson records decisions about disclosure, punishment, and mercy as well as feats of reasoning. The collection asks readers to consider what an investigator owes to a client, to the law, and to someone whose life a revelation could damage.

angleCards.title: Follow the evidence
angleCards.text: Keep track of what you actually see before Holmes explains it. Which details become clues, and which conclusions depend on assumptions about people?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to trace each deduction from the evidence given and distinguish observation from assumption.

angleCards.title: Listen to Watson
angleCards.text: Notice when Watson is amused, impressed, ashamed, or alarmed. His response shapes our view of Holmes and keeps the investigation attached to ordinary human feeling.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to follow Watson's changing responses and see how his storytelling shapes my judgement of Holmes.

angleCards.title: Watch the terms of dependence
angleCards.text: Attend to wages, inheritances, marriages, domestic arrangements, and employment contracts. Seemingly practical details reveal who controls another person's choices.
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to notice how money, class, gender, and household power create the conditions of each mystery.

angleCards.title: Ask what justice requires
angleCards.text: At the close of each case, consider who knows the truth and what is done with that knowledge. Does the outcome serve the client, the law, or a different idea of justice?
angleCards.angleObjective: I want to compare the stories' decisions about exposure, mercy, punishment, and the limits of the law.

cast.name: Sherlock Holmes
cast.description: From his rooms in Baker Street, Holmes investigates problems that defeat or fall outside routine police work. Close observation, disguise, and carefully staged encounters are among his methods.

cast.name: Dr. Watson
cast.description: A doctor and Holmes's former fellow lodger, Watson records the cases and often assists with them. His medical practice and marriage give him a domestic life beyond Baker Street.

cast.name: Irene Adler
cast.role: The woman in the opening case
cast.description: A former opera singer living in London, Adler becomes the focus of an investigation involving a photograph and a royal client's reputation.

cast.name: Jabez Wilson
cast.description: A red-haired shopkeeper whose unusually generous copying job ends without explanation. He brings the strange history of the Red-headed League to Holmes.

cast.name: Mary Sutherland
cast.description: A young woman who asks Holmes to investigate the disappearance of Hosmer Angel. Her account connects courtship, family authority, and financial independence.

cast.name: Helen Stoner
cast.description: In The Speckled Band, Helen seeks help with fears connected to her family home and her sister's death.

cast.name: Violet Hunter
cast.description: In The Copper Beeches, an offer of unusually high wages comes with unusual demands. Violet consults Holmes about whether to accept it.
